description: Per race name, count every driver standings record. Compare those counts with their average across names and summarise the names that are above average.

a.request: Linking driver standings to races by race id (and dropping standings with no matching race), work out for each race name (`races.name`) the average season-to-date championship points (`driverStandings.points`, ignoring missing values) and the number of driver standings records under that name. Take the average of that count across all race names, and keep only the race names whose count is strictly above it. Return a single row with three values: the average of those race names' average points, the average of their counts, and the average amount by which their count exceeds the overall average count. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT r.name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_pts, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), t AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_pts) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(g.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(g.cnt - t.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM g, t WHERE g.cnt > t.avg_cnt

c.request: Using driver standings linked to their races by race id (leaving out standings with no matching race), for each race name (`races.name`) get the average season-to-date championship points (`driverStandings.points`, ignoring missing values) and how big its standings field is. Then focus on the race names whose field size is strictly above the average field size across all race names. In one row, give the average of their average points, their average field size, and how far above the overall average their field size is on average. No rounding. Per race name, count every driver standings record. Compare those counts with their average across names and summarise the names that are above average.
c.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT r.name AS name, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points, COUNT(*) AS field_size FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(field_size) AS avg_field FROM per) SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(p.field_size) AS avg_field_size, AVG(p.field_size - o.avg_field) AS avg_excess_over_overall FROM per p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.field_size > o.avg_field

b.request: For each race name, count all of its driver standings records (joined to races by raceId) and average its non-null points. Then keep the race names whose count is strictly above the average count across all race names. For those, return in one row the average of their average points, the average of their counts, and the average amount by which their counts exceed the overall average count, with no rounding
b.sql: WITH per_race AS (SELECT r.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS cnt, AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM per_race) SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points, AVG(p.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(p.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM per_race p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.cnt > o.avg_cnt

d.request: For each race name (`races.name`), count all of its driver standings records, including those with missing points, by linking driverStandings to races on race id and leaving out standings with no matching race. Then compute the average of those counts across all race names. Finally, summarise the race names whose count is strictly above that average.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT r.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name) SELECT name, cnt FROM counts WHERE cnt > (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM counts) ORDER BY cnt DESC, name
